body.statement: For every compact \(\mathcal K=[\kappa_-,\kappa_+]\), count cutoff \(K\), and endpoint mesh \(h\), \(\overline D_{\mathrm{det}}(\mathcal K)\le D_{K,h}(\mathcal K)\le\overline D_{\mathrm{det}}(\mathcal K)+L\tau_K+2h\). At every fixed observed share, the finite-grid semi-infinite mixed-integer program admits a finite nuisance witness set whose integer optimum equals its continuum-nuisance optimum. Complete branch-and-bound with outward arithmetic therefore supplies a valid integer lower witness; a root linear-programming relaxation alone need not do so.
body.justification: This separates unconditional truncation and integrality control from the genuinely hard uniform-share covering step.
body.gap: Kabaila and Byrne (2001) give scalar exact enumeration and Schafer and Stark (2009) give convergent finite games; neither yields matching integer witnesses with an explicit outward error budget.
body.consumer: Auditors obtain finite, reproducible lower bounds and conservative upper policies rather than sampled-grid evidence or an unreported integrality gap.
